title: Isomorphisms on rational tangent spaces detect etaleness between smooth schemes
statement: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-field, def-weil-algebraic-closure], let $X$ and $Y$ be smooth schemes of finite type over $k$ [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], and let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism. For each $x\in X(k)$, let $df_x:T_{X/k,x}\to T_{Y/k,f(x)}$ be the tangent map [def-sc-scheme-tangent-space]. If $df_x$ is a $k$-linear isomorphism for every $x\in X(k)$, then $f$ is etale [def-weil-etale-morphism]. Empty schemes and disconnected schemes are allowed; no restriction is imposed on the characteristic of $k$.

source.place: Tag 02GU (lemma-etale-at-point), smooth-source and smooth-target tangent-isomorphism consequence; global detection by Tags 02J4 (lemma-enough-finite-type-points) and 01TB (lemma-jacobson-finite-type-points). The rational-point differential criterion is also stated in Milne, Algebraic Groups, printed p.267, before Lemma 13.35.

proof.text:
Fix $x\in X(k)$ and put $y=f(x)\in Y(k)$; their structural residue-field maps identify both residue fields with $k$. Write $R_z=\mathcal O_{Z,z}$, $\mathfrak m_z=\ker(R_z\to k)$ and $E_z=\Omega_{Z/k,z}\otimes_{R_z}k$ for $(Z,z)=(X,x),(Y,y)$. Here is the elementary differential-fibre comparison used below. On an affine chart the universal differential presentation [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and the definition [def-sc-relative-differential-sheaf] identify $E_z$ with $\Omega_{R_z/k}\otimes_{R_z}k$: localization sends $d(a/s)$ to $s^{-1}da-as^{-2}ds$, and this formula gives the inverse to localization of differentials. The maps
$$c_z:\mathfrak m_z/\mathfrak m_z^2\longrightarrow E_z,\quad[b]\longmapsto db\otimes1,\qquad c_z^{-1}(da\otimes\lambda)=\lambda[a-\bar a]$$
are well defined and inverse. Indeed $a\mapsto[a-\bar a]$ is a $k$-derivation into $\mathfrak m_z/\mathfrak m_z^2$ since $ab-\bar a\bar b\equiv\bar a(b-\bar b)+\bar b(a-\bar a)$ modulo $\mathfrak m_z^2$; the universal property gives the inverse, and the two composites fix the displayed generators. These formulas also show that $c_x,c_y$ commute with the local-ring map of $f$.

source.place: Tag 0B2E, first isomorphism, rational residue-field case; the explicit inverse uses the structural splitting k -> R_z -> k.

proof.text: Let $u:\mathfrak m_y/\mathfrak m_y^2\to\mathfrak m_x/\mathfrak m_x^2$ be induced by $f$. By [lem-sc-rational-tangent-cotangent-duality], $df_x$ is $u^*$, so $u^*$ is bijective. Its injectivity implies that $u$ is surjective by [lem-sc-dual-map-injective-iff-surjective]. If $u(b)=0$ and $b\ne0$, choose $\ell$ with $\ell(b)\ne0$ by [lem-weil-pbc-vector-space-dual-separates]. Surjectivity of $u^*$ writes $\ell=\psi\circ u$, contradicting $u(b)=0$. Thus $u$ is also injective. The comparisons of Step 1 therefore identify the pullback differential map $E_y\to E_x$, $da\otimes1\mapsto d(f^\sharp a)\otimes1$, with an isomorphism.

source.place: Tags 0B2E and 0B2F, cotangent description and naturality of tangent maps; dual-vector-space argument written out.

proof.text: Choose finite-type affine neighbourhoods $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ of $y$ and $W=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $x$ with $f(W)\subseteq V$. For this elementary shrinking, use the finite-type affine covers in [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], then a principal open of a source chart contained in $f^{-1}(V)$; if that chart has algebra $B_0$, its new algebra $(B_0)_s$ is still finitely generated, by adjoining $s^{-1}$. Both neighbourhoods are smooth over $k$, since smoothness is local on the source in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Choose algebra generators $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ of $A$. Their differentials span $E_y$: write every element of $A$ as a polynomial in the $a_i$ and apply the Leibniz rule; passage to the stalk and fibre uses the localization formula of Step 1. Choose a subfamily $h_1,\ldots,h_d$ of the $a_i$ whose differential classes form a basis, allowing $d=0$. By Step 2, the classes of $d(f^*h_j)$ form a basis of $E_x$. Thus the morphisms $h_Y:V\to\mathbf A^d_k$ with coordinates $h_j$ and $h_X:W\to\mathbf A^d_k$ with coordinates $f^*h_j$ satisfy $h_X=h_Y\circ f|_W$.

source.place: Tag 01T1, finite-type affine charts; the chosen-coordinate setup for Tag 02GU (8). Polynomial differentiation and selecting a basis from a finite spanning list are elementary.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-etale-at-point-from-differentials] to $(V,y,h_1,\ldots,h_d)$ and to $(W,x,f^*h_1,\ldots,f^*h_d)$. Both schemes are smooth and finite type over the field $k$, and Step 3 verifies the respective differential-basis hypotheses. We obtain neighbourhoods $V'\subseteq V$ and $W'\subseteq W$ on which $h_Y$ and $h_X$ are etale. Set $U_x=W'\cap f^{-1}(V')$. The restriction $h_X|_{U_x}$ is etale, since its factorization through $W'$ is an open immersion followed by an etale map, by parts (1),(2) of [lem-weil-pbc-etale-composition-cancellation]. It equals $(h_Y|_{V'})\circ(f|_{U_x}:U_x\to V')$. Part (3) of that node gives etaleness of $U_x\to V'$. Composing with the open immersion $V'\to Y$ and using parts (1),(2) again shows $f|_{U_x}:U_x\to Y$ is etale. In particular $U_x$ is an open neighbourhood of the original rational point $x$.

source.place: Tag 02GU (8) via the existing prescribed-coordinate lemma (Tags 01V7 and 00T7); Tags 02GP, 02GN and 02GW for open immersions, composition and cancellation.

proof.text: Let $O=\bigcup_{x\in X(k)}U_x$. It contains every rational point. If $z$ is a finite type point of $X$, apply [lem-sfb-finite-type-field-point-characterization] to the canonical finite-type morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(z)\to X$. It gives an affine open neighbourhood $Z$ in which $z$ is closed. This open subscheme is locally of finite type over $k$ by the affine-local definition [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Applying [lem-weil-pbc-closed-point-residue-field-base] to $Z\to\operatorname{Spec}k$, with $k$ algebraically closed, gives $k\simeq\kappa(z)$ as structural fields. Thus $z$ comes from a $k$-point of $X$ and lies in $O$. The conclusion of [lem-sfb-finite-type-points-detect-open] is therefore $O=|X|$. Finally the neighbourhoods $U_x$ cover $X$, and their restrictions of $f$ are etale by Step 4, so [lem-weil-pbc-etale-local-on-source] gives that $f$ is etale. If $X$ is empty the same argument uses the empty open cover; varying $d$ with $x$ permits disconnected schemes. None of the steps restricts the characteristic.

source.place: Tags 01TA, 02J4 and 01TB, with algebra.tex Tag 00FV for algebraically closed residue fields; Tag 02GJ for locality of etaleness.

proof_origin.place: Explicit rational cotangent and chosen-coordinate proof of the 02GU smooth tangent consequence, assembled from varieties.tex Tags 0B2E/0B2F, the existing 02GU/01V7/00T7 coordinate criterion, 02GW cancellation, and 01TA/02J4/02GJ point detection/locality. Etale permanence restricts the two coordinate maps, cancels their common etale target map, and composes with the target open immersion; generic permanence.

U_x = W' ∩ f^{-1}(V') contains x; open-immersion/composition/cancellation give that f|U_x is étale, and no affineness of the intersection is used. lean.statement: theorem etale_of_bijective_rational_tangentMap (k : Type u) [Field k] [IsAlgClosed k] (X Y : Scheme.{u}) (pX : X ⟶ Spec (.of k)) (pY : Y ⟶ Spec (.of k)) [Smooth pX] [LocallyOfFiniteType pX] [QuasiCompact pX] [Smooth pY] [LocallyOfFiniteType pY] [QuasiCompact pY] (f : X ⟶ Y) (hf : f ≫ pY = pX) (hdf : ∀ x : X, Function.Bijective (pX.residueFieldMap x).hom → ∃ he : Function.Bijective (f.residueFieldMap x).hom, Function.Bijective (schemeTangentMap k X Y pX pY f hf x he)) : Etale f
